scenes.title: ALTER TABLE
scenes.narration: ALTER TABLE changes an existing table's structure without recreating it from scratch.

scenes.title: Modifying structure
bullets: Can change a column's data type
scenes.narration: ALTER TABLE lets you add, drop, or rename columns on a table that already exists. It can also change a column's data type when your needs evolve. Constraints can be added or removed the same way, all without rebuilding the table.

scenes.title: Adding a column
scenes.code:
ALTER TABLE customers
ADD COLUMN phone VARCHAR(20);
scenes.narration: This statement targets the existing customers table for modification. The ADD COLUMN clause introduces a new phone column typed as a short string. Existing rows receive a NULL phone value until they are updated.

scenes.title: Applying a change
scenes.narration: You name the table you want to change and describe the modification. The database then updates the schema definition accordingly. Existing data adapts, for example with new columns starting out as NULL.

scenes.text: ALTER TABLE evolves your schema safely as requirements change over time.
scenes.narration: Use ALTER TABLE to evolve a table in place as requirements shift, avoiding the disruption of dropping and rebuilding it.
